name: Medicine shortages
summary: UK pharmacists say shortages hit up to 6.4m items a month; a flood-hit plant may prolong US chemo shortages to 2028
state: On 17 Nov the National Pharmacy Association estimated shortages could affect up to 6.4 million prescription items a month in 2026 (Pharmaceutical Journal). In the US, ASHP counted 225 active shortages in the third quarter, with cancer drug shortages worsening (Becker's Hospital Review), and a flood-damaged plant may prolong chemotherapy shortages to 2028 (CancerNetwork, 2 Nov). Shortages span several countries but no widespread rationing across major health systems was found on 22 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: If a pharmacy cannot supply a medicine, speak to the pharmacist or GP about alternatives; do not stop treatment without advice. NHS guidance covers Serious Shortage Protocols that let pharmacists substitute.
rubric_hit: Essential medicine shortages across several countries = Watch; no widespread rationing

sources.title: Pharmaceutical Journal — NPA urges government action on medicines shortages
Becker's Hospital Review — Cancer drug shortages worsen: notes from ASHP's Q3 report
CancerNetwork — Flood-damaged plant may prolong US chemotherapy shortages to 2028

why: Shipping disruption, factory failures and export curbs can leave essential medicines short, as with US IV fluids after Hurricane Helene in 2024.
drivers: Manufacturing concentrated in India and China, shipping, raw materials, demand spikes, regulation.

rubric.alert: Shortages forcing widespread rationing or cancelled treatment across major health systems.
rubric.watch: A shortage of an essential medicine or supply across several countries, or a UK Serious Shortage Protocol for a widely used medicine.
rubric.normal: No widespread shortages of essential medicines in major health systems.
